Job Description BAE Systems is seeking a talented, motivated Computer/Software Engineering internship candidate who wants to join a team at a dynamic company that values your technical excellence. At our Space Systems facility in Manassas, VA we develop and produce a wide array of space products, from single-board radiation hardened computers to complete space payloads, for commercial, military, and space communities. The company specializes in radiation-hardened electronics and space applications, including application-specific integrated circuits, memories, and single-board computers. Our single-board computer products are flying on over 250 different spacecraft, including three generations of Mars rovers and Advanced Extremely High Frequency (AEHF) communication satellites.

The Software Engineering organization is responsible for the analysis, specification, planning, development, design, integration, testing, and production of embedded software and test solutions for our prime mission equipment. We support the definition of SW/test architectures and designs that achieve "best value" goals for meeting performance and life cycle requirements within allocated budget and schedule constraints, while maintaining consistency with established company practices and methods. The organization supports concurrent engineering with specialty disciplines to define software and test requirements, designs, and products. As a software intern, you will have the opportunity to work on a variety of projects, collaborating with our experienced engineers to design, develop, and deploy software solutions. This is an excellent opportunity to gain hands-on experience in software development, learn from industry experts, and contribute to the development of cutting-edge technology.

We offer a supportive environment that allows you to continue to learn via training and mentoring, and advance your technical skills through performing assigned responsibilities which may include:
• Developing embedded software for Board Support Packages (BSP) and Start-up ROM (SUROM)
• Developing automated test software in a variety of languages
• Supporting technical work in areas ranging from the design, verification, test of space products and systems
• Collaborating with cross-functional teams to identify and prioritize project requirements
• Participating in integration activities of production test systems
• Participating in code reviews and contribute to the improvement of the codebase
• Generating, reviewing and updating the technical content of drawings, engineering specifications, reports, and other documents associated with the engineering process
• Troubleshooting and debugging software or test-related issues

Cross Department work sharing may lead to performing work in system or processor design and simulation, lab test and debug, or software engineering activities related to operational and test software.Required Education, Experience, & Skills • Enrolled in a bachelor's or master's Degree program in Computer, Software or Electrical Engineering
• Proficiency with programming in C/C++
• Interest in embedded processors (Raspberry-Pi, Arduino, etc.)
• Interest is operating systems
• Ability to perform independent lab work with digital logic devices or components and circuit assemblies
• Ability to apply engineering principals to the development of software for special test equipment
• Ability to work with cross functional teams following established BAE Systems design processes
• Strong communications skills and ability to work independentlyPreferred Education, Experience, & Skills • Scripting and programming language familiarity: Visual Studio, Python, C#, LabWindows/CVI, Assembly
• Familiarity with embedded engineering applications
• Knowledge of PowerPC architecture
• Familiarity with electrical engineering principles such as logic compatibility, timing and signal integrity

Pay Information
Full-Time Salary Range: $45553 - $63330

Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.

Temporary employees generally are not eligible for BAE Systems benefits, but can elect to participate in the 401(k) savings plan. Temporary employees working 20+ hours per week are eligible for medical benefits, the employee assistance program, and business travel accident insurance.
About BAE Systems Electronic Systems BAE Systems, Inc. is the U.S. subsidiary of BAE Systems plc, an international defense, aerospace and security company which delivers a full range of products and services for air, land and naval forces, as well as advanced electronics, security, information technology solutions and customer support services. Improving the future and protecting lives is an ambitious mission, but it’s what we do at BAE Systems. Working here means using your passion and ingenuity where it counts – defending national security with breakthrough technology, superior products, and intelligence solutions. As you develop the latest technology and defend national security, you will continually hone your skills on a team—making a big impact on a global scale. At BAE Systems, you’ll find a rewarding career that truly makes a difference. Electronic Systems (ES) is the global innovator behind BAE Systems’ game-changing defense and commercial electronics. Exploiting every electron, we push the limits of what is possible, giving our customers the edge and our employees opportunities to change the world. Our products and capabilities can be found everywhere – from the depths of the ocean to the far reaches of space. At our core are more than 14,000 highly talented Electronic Systems employees with the brightest minds in the industry, we make an impact – for our customers and the communities we serve.

Our Purpose:
We are building a championship organization that serves our fans, community and business partners through world class sports and entertainment. We believe that Winning Matters, our Fans come first, with risk comes reward, great teams can achieve unimaginable results, honoring the Pacific Northwest is our duty and driving the business is our responsibility.

Since the team was awarded in 2018 through to our first puck drop in 2021, the Kraken brand has become one of the most recognized and beloved in the NHL. Playing at Climate Pledge Arena, the most sustainable arena in the world, we want to provide a memorable experience every night and make fans for life. Our joint foundation, One Roof Foundation aims to advance equity and sustainability by increasing opportunities to thrive for our most vulnerable young people and communities. Kraken Community Iceplex serves not only as the official practice facility for the team, but also as a thriving 3-sheet community facility providing skating and hockey programming for all.

Our Vision:
To inspire a passion for learning and empower future leaders in a safe environment where they are valued for their individuality and diverse capabilities.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion in Hiring:
The Seattle Kraken aspire to write a new playbook in sports and entertainment that includes everyone. In alignment with this vision, if you don’t meet every job requirement listed—or if you haven’t played ice hockey before or are still learning about the sport—we still encourage you to apply. We understand you may bring other relevant experiences and expertise to help us become the highest performance organization we can be. One of our core values is ‘Make Us Better’ and we recognize diversity, equity and inclusion as a critical business strategy.

If you’d like to request an accommodation in the application or interview process, please let us know by emailing: hr@seattlekraken.com.

Position Summary:
The Software Engineer Intern will have exposure to the end-to-end development of features within the Seattle Kraken + CPA (Climate Pledge Arena) app, including feature design, end-to-end architecture, development, manual and automated testing, and releasing app updates. This role will work closely with three engineers at the mid to senior level and VP, Digital Innovation and Fan Experience to shape fans’ digital access to the Kraken and other sports and events at Climate Pledge Arena. The ideal candidate has a strong technical foundation, communication skills, and a curiosity for the intersection of technology and the sports and events industry.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:
• Collaborate on ideation of new features and improvements to existing features in the Seattle Kraken + CPA app.
• Follow design documents, architecture diagrams, and technical specification documents.
• Write clean, maintainable code to add to the Seattle Kraken + CPA app codebase using React Native, JavaScript/TypeScript, and occasionally Swift and Kotlin.
• Assist in developing APIs and back-end services on AWS.
• Help prepare Seattle Kraken + CPA app updates for release on iOS and Android devices.
• Support the Digital Innovation and Fan Experience team in understanding app performance by reviewing app metrics and qualitative feedback from users.
• Participate in an Agile workflow, including sprint ceremonies like Retrospective, Sprint Planning, and a daily Scrum meeting.
• Shadow an engineer’s on-call experience once – responding to requests, monitoring app performance, and preparing for usage spikes around games and events.
• Other duties as assigned.

What You Will Learn:
• Industry-standard programming practices in a highly collaborative team.
• Overview of project management and technical project management.
• How to monitor app performance to identify and mitigate app problems.
• What it’s like to work in and support a fast-paced, highly visible professional sports environment.
• How small technical teams can maximize output and collaborate with non-technical teams.

Required Experience & Qualifications:
• Experience with data-structures and algorithms in a general-purpose programming language
• Ability to write clean, maintainable code prioritizing simplicity and reusability in a general-purpose programming language
• Ability to write basic test coverage
• Familiarity with version control
• Can translate between thought and written code
• Can apply feedback to iteratively improve their code
• An adaptable problem-solver and a strong verbal and written communicator.

Total Rewards Package:
• Compensation:
• In accordance with Washington’s Equal Pay and Opportunity Act, the pay range for the position is $21.50-$22.50/hr. Actual base pay will depend on the employee’s experience and other job-related factors permitted by law.
• Company-paid Orca card.
• Company-wide recognition platform.
• Corporate office located at the Kraken Community Iceplex in Northgate; within walking distance of the Northgate Light Rail Station and Northgate Transit Center; free parking.

Working Conditions:
• This role is based on-site in our Seattle office and requires work to be performed in person. However, we do value flexibility as the business will allow and offer occasional opportunities to work from home.
• This role will work approximately 20-30 hours per week. Hours may fluctuate based on school schedule, work assigned, etc.
• Must be able to work a flexible schedule inclusive of weekends, nights and holidays required.
• Frequent bending, lifting 15-20 pounds, sitting, exposure to multiple external elements, extensive walking through the building including inclines and stairs.
• Must have transportation to and from events.

MITRE is different from most technology companies. We are a not-for-profit corporation chartered to work for the public interest, with no commercial conflicts to influence what we do. The R&D centers we operate for the government create lasting impact in fields as diverse as cybersecurity, healthcare, aviation, defense, and enterprise transformation. We're making a difference every day—working for a safer, healthier, and more secure nation and world. Our workplace reflects our values. Job Description

MITRE delivers to its customers the full spectrum of software development capabilities from prototyping, through architecture and modeling, to software assessments. We prototype new capabilities and deliver advanced experimental functionality to address unmet business and mission needs. 

As a recent graduate working in software engineering or computer science, you will work with a team to apply your knowledge and gain experience with one or more of the following: 
• Front-end, back-end, middleware or full-stack software development
• Artificial intelligence
• Cyber software
• DevSecOps
• Mobile computing
• Embedded systems and Internet of Things
• Modeling and simulation
• Model-based engineering
• Game theory and design/virtual reality

Basic Qualifications
• Must have a Bachelor’s, Master’s or PhD degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science or a related degree.
• "Hands-on" skills in at least one or more programming language
• Exposure to software development tools and frameworks, including source control management tools (e.g., Git)
• Familiarity with software development methodologies
• Sustained excellence in academic performance

 Preferred Qualifications
• Experience having applied computer science learning to an internship or research/lab position.
• Knowledge of software design patterns
• Knowledge of database technologies, including relational or NoSQL
• Demonstrated interest in serving the public

Clearance: In addition to passing MITRE’s employment background check, you may be submitted for a U.S. Government Security clearance.  This is determined by the Department of Defense’s adjudicative guidelines for receiving a clearance, to include U.S. citizenship. Job Summary:
Provides direct nursing care in settings where patients require complex assessments and intervention, in accordance with established policies, procedures and protocols of the healthcare organization.

Job Responsibilities and Requirements:

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES
• Obtains comprehensive data pertinent to the patient from the patient, family other healthcare providers to develop a holistic picture of the patient’s needs or condition.
• Analyzes and synthesizes data from the assessment in determining diagnosis or conditions relevant to care.
• Identifies optimal outcomes for the patient in collaboration with the patient, family and interprofessional team.
• Develops a plan that prescribes strategies and alternatives to attain outcomes, using clinical judgement in collaboration with patient, family and interprofessional care team.
• Implements the plan, employing strategies to promote and maintain a safe environment, coordinates implementation with patient, family and interprofessional team.
• Evaluates processes and progress toward attainment of goals and outcomes.
• Contributes to the quality and effectiveness of nursing practice, evaluates their own practice, and maintains current knowledge and competence.
• Communicates effectively in all areas of practice, collaborates with patient, family and interprofessional team.
• Uses clinical inquiry and integrates best evidence into practice.
• Applies the existing body of evidence-based practice and scientific knowledge in health care to critical care nursing practice, ensuring that nursing care is delivered based on patient’s age-specific needs and clinical needs as described in the department's Scope of Service.
• Works in a constant state of alertness and safe manner.
• Performs other duties as assigned.

EDUCATION
• Graduate of accredited school of nursing or education equivalency for licensing

EXPERIENCE
• No experience required

• Constant use of speech to share information through oral communication.
• Constant standing and walking.

• Frequent use of hearing to receive oral communication, distinguish body sounds and/or hear alarms, malfunctioning machinery, etc.
• Occasional lifting/carrying and pushing/pulling objects weighing 25-50 lbs.
• Occasional lifting/moving of patients.
• Occasional bending, stooping, kneeling, squatting, twisting, gripping and repetitive foot/leg and hand/arm movements.
• Occasional driving.
• Rare crawling and running.

Job Summary:

The Level I Novice Registered Nurse is an entry-level nurse who has graduated from an accredited nursing program and does not have clinical experience as a Registered Nurse. The Level I MWHC nurse is responsible for mastering the knowledge and skills necessary for competent Level II nursing practice within one year of beginning employment at Mary Washington Healthcare.

Practice Standards for a Level I Registered Nurse:

In the MWHC Practice Standards, a Level I Registered Nurse is outlined in the following areas of:
• Exemplary Professional Practice Standards
• Structural Empowerment Practice Standards
• Transformational Leadership Practice Standards
• New Knowledge, Innovations, and Improvement Practice Standards

Essential Functions & Responsibilities:
• Direct and coordinate nursing care, including oversight of licensed and unlicensed personnel in any assigned or delegated tasks using the nursing process and interdisciplinary teamwork to achieve desired patient outcomes.
• Coordinate involvement of the patient, family and health team members in patient care, including patient/family teaching and discharge planning.
• Communicate and coordinate the plan of care and other pertinent information to/from other health care team members.
• Assist Leadership to define standards of excellence for patient care; participate in improvement of patient care services.
• Participate in, contribute to and integrate performance improvement into care delivery and participate in quality improvement activities.
• Participate in daily operational activities necessary for safe patient/staff environment.
• Provide input to the Nurse Manager regarding unit needs.
• Participate in unit, departmental and hospital committees for formulation of nursing and hospital policies and procedures.
• Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications:
• Graduate of an accredited nursing program and has no experience as a Registered Nurse.
• Valid RN License from Virginia or reciprocal compact state.
• BSN is preferred.
• AHA BLS Provider CPR required at hire.
• AHA ACLS Provider required within 1 year.
• NIHSS (Bluecloud) required within 90 days

We are seeking a highly motivated software engineer intern to join our program for Summer 2026. You will work on a team that is the Lead System Integrator, responsible for engineering, hardware and software integration, test, deployment, and training. The software intern will support the software integration and test scrum team, gaining practical experience by applying software engineering skills learned in college.

This is an onsite role at the RTX Sterling, VA, office, working onsite five days a week.

What YOU will do:
• You will be a member of the software integration and test scrum team, which is responsible for integrating and testing multiple software applications using automated test methods
• Support the development and execution of automated test cases to test system requirements, using tools such as Python/Nifi/Playwright (automated functional and interface testing) and Jmeter (performance testing)
• Actively participate in the project’s Agile process, including sprint planning, daily scrums, and end of sprint demonstrations and retrospectives
• You will be working collaboratively onsite in our Sterling, VA facility.

Qualification You Must Have:
• This position is for a college summer intern who is enrolled in a Bachelor’s (or higher) degree program in Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) and will be at minimum Junior year by summer 2026.
• Experience with programming languages such as Python, Java, JavaScript
• U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are authorized to access information under this program/contract.

Qualifications We Prefer:
• Completion of software projects as part of coursework, part-time employment, and/or personal projects
• Experience using disciplined development processes in a team environment
• Demonstrated ability to work effectively with colleagues and leaders in a team environment
• Participation in Raytheon’s Future Ready Engineers program or similar STEM talent development program

Collins Aerospace, a Raytheon Technologies company, is a leader in technologically advanced and intelligent solutions for the global aerospace and defense industry. Collins Aerospace has the capabilities, comprehensive portfolio and expertise to solve customers’ toughest challenges and to meet the demands of a rapidly evolving global market.

Do you want to be a part of something bigger? A team whose impact stretches across the world, and even beyond? At Collins Aerospace, our Mission Systems team helps civilian, military and government customers complete their most complex missions — whatever and wherever they may be.
